body.x: Leather and suede shoes are normally sent to a cleaner because they cannot be washed at home.

AiRET Inc, a smart home hardware developer focused on the entryway and led by CEO Bon-Ung Koo, exhibited the AX1 at the 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026), held from Oct. 13 to 16 at COEX in Seoul. The AX1 is a fully automatic household shoe cleaner that does not immerse shoes in water. At the show, AiRET received an Innovation Award in the AI transformation (AX) category, alongside recipients including Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics. The company says it came with two goals: to widen contact with domestic home appliance distribution channels and to identify B2B adopters in hotels and residential developments.

The user places the shoes inside and closes the door, and the whole process from recognition to cleaning runs automatically. Vision AI embedded in the device identifies the type and material of each pair and determines the cleaning conditions on its own, so the user never selects a material setting or adjusts cleaning intensity. Because shoes are not submerged, AiRET says materials such as leather and suede can be handled at home.

At its booth, the company showed a full-scale 1:1 model that revealed the internal structure and the cleaning sequence, and ran continuous docent sessions explaining how the product works and the thinking behind its design. It will reflect the domestic feedback gathered at KES 2026 in its CES exhibit in January 2027.

AiRET started its business in 2024 and incorporated in April 2025. Three of its six employees work in research and development. It has received transfers of four patented technologies from a major Korean corporation and a public institution and applies them in product development. In 2026, it was selected for the NIPA's High-Performance Computing Support Program and received an H100 GPU, which it uses to train its shoe recognition models. It also won a CES 2026 Innovation Award and has confirmed its participation in Eureka Park at CES 2027.

body.x: The AX1 is in the final stage before mass production, and AiRET has no formal export sales yet. It has signed a proof-of-concept (PoC) agreement for product adoption with a luxury homebuilder based in Las Vegas. In August 2026, it took part in THECA 2026 in Bangkok at the official invitation of the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI), where it identified local distribution and supply chain partners. In Korea, it has been selected for the Korea Institute of Design Promotion's Style (Design) Tech program and the Federation of Korean Entrepreneurs' Plus Startup program.

AiRET's priority markets are North America and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates. In North America, it cites the high proportion of detached housing, which creates demand for shoe care around entryways and garages, and the practice of building appliances into new homes, which makes entry through homebuilders viable. It chose Dubai because the custom of removing shoes indoors gives it a demand structure for entryway products similar to Korea's, because sand and dust from the desert climate make shoe cleaning a constant need, and because active construction of luxury villas and residences, with strong purchasing power for premium appliances, supports the price of an early-entry product. It also sees Dubai as a base for expanding across the GCC region.

The company is looking for local distributors of premium home appliances, homebuilders and interior contractors that install appliances in new housing, and hotel and residence operators able to adopt the product room by room. It gives priority to partners that can handle installation and after-sales service in addition to distribution.

AiRET's immediate goal is to take part in CES in January 2027 and introduce the product formally to the North American market. It is also prioritizing mass production for a domestic launch and converting the PoC agreement with the U.S. homebuilder into actual supply. In Dubai, it aims to find local distribution partners and hotel and residence operators and ship its first export volume during 2027. It plans to offer the freestanding AX1 alongside a built-in model, for general households and new residential construction respectively.

The 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026) ran from Oct. 13 (Tuesday) to 16 (Friday) in Halls A and B at COEX in Seoul. The Korea Electronics Association (KEA) organized the show, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources hosted it. The KES website lists 500 exhibitors and 1,100 booths. Its themes included electronic parts and materials such as sensors, connectors, printed circuit boards (PCBs) and power supplies; AI transformation (AX) fields such as generative AI, on-device AI, AI chips and smart home and wearable devices; mobility; robotics; digital health; ESG; and Web 3.0 and XR. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event featured X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony took place on Oct. 13.
